title: Twists are well-defined on the common-finite-stage coefficient category
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime, let $S$ be a scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], fix $m\in\mathbf Z$, and let $\mathcal C_S=D^b_c(S,\Qlb)$ be the common-stage category of [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. For each finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ contained in $\Qlb$, let $T_{E,m}$ be the rational twist functor induced on integral representatives by tensoring with $\mathcal O_E(m)$ [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. Assume the finite-stage inverse identities $T_{E,-m}T_{E,m}\cong\mathrm{id}$ and $T_{E,m}T_{E,-m}\cong\mathrm{id}$ given by line evaluation. Write $B_{F/E}$ for scalar extension from $E$ to $F$ [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], and use the natural comparisons $\beta_{F/E,C}:B_{F/E}(T_{E,m}C)\xrightarrow{\sim}T_{F,m}(B_{F/E}C)$ of [lem-weil-integral-twist-derived-scalar] after rationalization. Assume their identity and tower compatibility of [lem-weil-integral-twist-scalar-coherence] and their compatibility with line evaluation of [lem-weil-integral-twist-base-change], for $m$ and $-m$. Then the assignment $(E,C)\mapsto(E,T_{E,m}C)$ defines a functor on $\mathcal C_S$: for a representative $[F,f]:(E,C)\to(E',C')$, where $f:B_{F/E}C\to B_{F/E'}C'$, its image is represented by
$$
 [F,\,\beta_{F/E',C'}^{-1}\circ T_{F,m}(f)\circ\beta_{F/E,C}].
$$
Equivalently it is $[F,T_{F,m}(f)]$ after identifying the endpoints by $\beta$. This class is independent of enlarging $F$, and composition is preserved. The line-evaluation inverse identities descend through these same comparisons. The resulting functor $T_m:\mathcal C_S\to\mathcal C_S$ has inverse $T_{-m}$, so $\Qlb(m)$ is invertible in the common-stage category.

source.place: Proof, final sentence: twists at common finite stages; representative-independence and descent of inverse twist functors in returned item step 9.

proof.text:
Write $B_{F/E}$ for the transitions and $a_{G/F,E,C}:B_{G/F}B_{F/E}C\xrightarrow{\sim}B_{G/E}C$ for their canonical composition maps [lem-weil-scalar-extension-composition]. Suppress only the canonical identity-extension unitors. For a fixed common stage $F$, put $X=B_{F/E}C$, $Y=B_{F/E'}C'$ and $b_C=\beta_{F/E,C}$, $b_{C'}=\beta_{F/E',C'}$. The supplied natural comparisons of [lem-weil-integral-twist-derived-scalar] are used after the rationalization [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], exactly as assumed in the statement. Define
$$t_F(f)=b_{C'}^{-1}\circ T_{F,m}(f)\circ b_C.$$
Its source is $B_{F/E}(T_{E,m}C)$ and its target is $B_{F/E'}(T_{E',m}C')$, so it represents a morphism between the asserted image objects. Naturality of each comparison holds for the rationalized morphisms as part of the hypotheses; no construction with an infinite coefficient ring is being used.

source.place: Final sentence, common finite stages: typing the representative formula

proof.text:
Fix $F\subset G$ and abbreviate $B=B_{G/F}$, $T=T_{G,m}$, $a_C=a_{G/F,E,C}$, $a_{TC}=a_{G/F,E,T_{E,m}C}$ and $d_C=\beta_{G/E,C}$. The tower equation of [lem-weil-integral-twist-scalar-coherence], after rationalization, is
$$T(a_C)\circ\beta_{G/F,X}\circ B(b_C)=d_C\circ a_{TC}.$$
Consequently
$$B(b_C)\circ a_{TC}^{-1}=\beta_{G/F,X}^{-1}\circ T(a_C)^{-1}\circ d_C,$$
and, for the target object,
$$a_{TC'}\circ B(b_{C'}^{-1})=d_{C'}^{-1}\circ T(a_{C'})\circ\beta_{G/F,Y}.$$
These equalities follow by composing the tower equation with the displayed inverse isomorphisms on the indicated sides. They apply to $m$ and also to $-m$.

source.place: Final sentence, common finite stages: tower equations with endpoints retained

proof.text:
In the Hom system of [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], the enlargement of $f$ is $f^G=a_{C'}\circ B(f)\circ a_C^{-1}$. The enlargement of $t_F(f)$ is $a_{TC'}\circ B(t_F(f))\circ a_{TC}^{-1}$. Substitute the two equalities of Step 2 and use naturality
$$\beta_{G/F,Y}\circ B(T_{F,m}(f))=T(B(f))\circ\beta_{G/F,X}$$
of [lem-weil-integral-twist-derived-scalar]. The adjacent inverse factors cancel, giving
$$a_{TC'}B(t_F(f))a_{TC}^{-1}=d_{C'}^{-1}T(a_{C'})T(B(f))T(a_C)^{-1}d_C=t_G(f^G).$$
Thus twisting commutes with every enlargement. If two representatives at different stages determine the same class, the cited definition says that their enlargements agree at one further finite common stage. Apply this equality there to see that their twisted representatives also agree. This proves independence of representatives, including arbitrary enlargements.

source.place: Final sentence, common finite stages: representative independence by an explicit transport equality

proof.text:
At a common stage $F$, an identity is represented by $\mathrm{id}_{B_{F/E}C}$, and $t_F(\mathrm{id})=b_C^{-1}\mathrm{id}\,b_C=\mathrm{id}$. For composable representatives, enlarge both to a common $F$, as allowed by [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], and write $b_C,b_{C'},b_{C''}$ for the three comparisons. Then
$$t_F(g)\circ t_F(f)=b_{C''}^{-1}T_{F,m}(g)b_{C'}b_{C'}^{-1}T_{F,m}(f)b_C=b_{C''}^{-1}T_{F,m}(g\circ f)b_C=t_F(g\circ f).$$
Step 3 makes this calculation independent of that enlargement. This defines $T_m$ as a functor. Running the same construction with $-m$ defines $T_{-m}$.

source.place: Final sentence, common finite stages: identity and composition at a common finite stage

proof.text:
Let $e_{E,C}:T_{E,-m}T_{E,m}C\xrightarrow{\sim}C$ denote the assumed natural line-evaluation inverse identity. For $E\subset F$ define the comparison for this composite by
$$\gamma_{F/E,C}=T_{F,-m}(\beta^{m}_{F/E,C})\circ\beta^{-m}_{F/E,T_{E,m}C}.$$
Its source is $B_{F/E}(T_{E,-m}T_{E,m}C)$ and its target is $T_{F,-m}T_{F,m}(B_{F/E}C)$. Evaluation compatibility, assumed in the statement using [lem-weil-integral-twist-base-change], says precisely
$$e_{F,B_{F/E}C}\circ\gamma_{F/E,C}=B_{F/E}(e_{E,C}).$$
Indeed, the two paths tensor $C$ with the two opposite twist lines, extend coefficients, and evaluate the two line factors; the cited compatibility with evaluation equates these paths. The rationalization of [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] preserves this equality, since it preserves composition and identities. Interchanging $m$ and $-m$ gives the same equation for the other assumed evaluation $e'_{E,C}:T_{E,m}T_{E,-m}C\xrightarrow{\sim}C$.

source.place: Final sentence, common finite stages: evaluation compatibility for the composite twist

proof.text:
For each $(E,C)$ take the common-stage class of $e_{E,C}$. Its enlargement to $F$ is represented by $B_{F/E}(e_{E,C})=e_{F,X}\gamma_{F/E,C}$ by Step 5. Expanding twice the representative formula of Step 1 shows that $T_{-m}T_m([F,f])$ is represented by
$$\gamma_{F/E',C'}^{-1}\circ T_{F,-m}T_{F,m}(f)\circ\gamma_{F/E,C}.$$
Multiplying this expression on the left by $B_{F/E'}(e_{E',C'})$ gives
$$e_{F,Y}T_{F,-m}T_{F,m}(f)\gamma_{F/E,C}=f\,e_{F,X}\gamma_{F/E,C}=f\,B_{F/E}(e_{E,C}),$$
by naturality of the assumed finite-stage $e_F$. This is the required naturality square on common-stage classes [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. Every component is invertible: the class of $e_{E,C}^{-1}$ is its inverse, since their composites are identities already at stage $E$. Hence $T_{-m}T_m\cong\mathrm{id}$. Using $e'$ and reversing the two signs in the displayed computation gives $T_mT_{-m}\cong\mathrm{id}$.

source.place: Final sentence, common finite stages: descent and naturality of both inverse identities

proof.text: The object $\Qlb(m)$ of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed] is represented by $E(m)=T_{E,m}(E_S)$, and $\Qlb(-m)$ by $E(-m)$. At this finite stage the assumed line evaluations identify both ordered tensor products $E(m)\otimes_E^L E(-m)$ and $E(-m)\otimes_E^L E(m)$ with the coefficient unit $E_S$. Step 5 proves that these evaluations commute with scalar extension. Their classes are therefore the two inverse tensor identifications in the common-stage interpretation of the cited definition. This proves the asserted invertibility of $\Qlb(m)$, with inverse $\Qlb(-m)$.

source.place: Final sentence, common finite stages: invertibility of the common-stage twist line

Step 3: with β_{G/F} naturality the enlargement of t_F(f) equals t_G(f^G), which gives representative independence. Step 4: identity and composition hold. Step 6: expanding twice gives γ'^{-1}T_{-m}T_m(f)γ, and the naturality square and inverse components follow. Step 7: E(m)=T_{E,m}(E_S), and invertibility at Q̄ is read as in the parent's statement. Edge cases m=0, m<0, E=E', F=E and unrelated E, E' all go through.
